guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: The Company is raising 2026 GAAP EPS to be in the range of $5.45 to $5.85, from a prior range of $4.60 to $5.45. The Company is also raising and tightening the adjusted EPS* range to $5.95 to $6.25, from a prior range of $5.20 to $5.80. These ranges represent year over year growth of 113% and 31%, respectively, at the midpoint of each range as compared to 2025 performance. Free cash flow* is now expected to be in the range of $1.0 billion to $1.2 billion, revised from $600 million to $800 million, which incorporates the tariff refund realized year-to-date and projected taxes and fees associated with the CAM divestiture. The Company will discuss underlying assumptions on the earnings call.
1 Includes IEEPA tariff refund gain partially offset by directly attributable variable incentive compensation costs, growth investments, and taxes (for EPS only)
* Non-GAAP financial measure, as further defined in the Non-GAAP Financial Measures section below

The difference between the GAAP and Adjusted EPS* assumption range is approximately $0.40 to $0.50, consisting primarily of charges related to footprint actions and other cost actions, partially offset by the gain on the sale of the CAM business and related tax impact.

desk.headline: Adjusted EPS $2.31, well above estimates thanks partly to tariff refunds; 2026 EPS and cash-flow outlook raised
results: Sales were flat at $3.7bn (down 1%) after selling the aerospace fasteners business, but rose 4% on a like-for-like basis on stronger US tool sales.
Refunds of earlier import tariffs added about $0.67 a share and about 4.3 points of gross margin.
Tools & Outdoor sales rose 2% to $3.3bn, with segment margin up to 17.0%; Engineered Fastening sales fell 21%, with weak car-industry demand.
Free cash flow was $585m; the company bought back $250m of shares and approved a new $1bn buyback.

guidance.summary: Stanley Black & Decker raised its 2026 EPS and free cash flow ranges. The outlook does not count any further tariff refunds in the fourth quarter.

points: The CFO said about 3.5 points of the gross margin gain came from productivity and product mix, not refunds.
Most tariff refunds with a clear government process have now been received.
The company is bringing $70–80m of growth spending planned for 2027 into 2026, mainly on brands and marketing.
The CEO pointed to strength in US retail and professional channels and to new products driving growth.
call.source: Press release (Exhibit 99.1) and CFO Dive, 4 Nov 2026

watch: Underlying profit once the one-off tariff refunds fade.
Whether volume growth holds up while prices are falling 2–3%.
Car-industry demand in Engineered Fastening and the pace of the new $1bn buyback.

sources.title: Stanley Black & Decker raises EPS outlook after tariff refund boost — CFO Dive, 4 Nov 2026
